messages:
IncidentBot: HIGH: billing-metering pipeline alerted for token-count drift + delayed emits. Severity: P1. Symptoms: aggregated token counts diverging from raw ingest (~8-12% delta), outgoing overage flags being emitted. Affected region: us-west-2. Pager -> oncall. Link: https://dash.redwoodinc/realtime/alerts/2681234567

Priya K: on it. joining bridge now. @Marcus B can you check aggregator commit lag / consumer offsets? any recent deploys to metering-aggregator?

Marcus B: yep saw the alert. no deploys in the last 6h. quick check: ingest events arriving, consumer lag growing on aggregator-agg-01. looks like periodic backpressure causing missed windowing. sample counts (30m):
```
# raw ingest count: 1,230,412 tokens
# agg committed count: 1,132,098 tokens
# delta: 98,314 (7.99%)
```

Marcus B: digging into redis offsets and commit checkpoints. running consumer offset query now:
```
$ ./tools/consumer_offset_check --group=metering-agg --topic=usage-events
agg-01: lag=12456, state=RUNNING, last_commit=2681234000
agg-02: lag=128, state=RUNNING, last_commit=2681234560
```

Priya K: agg-01 lag 12k is the culprit. is agg-01 CPU / IO saturated? @Sam R can you grab infra metrics and the pod logs?

Sam R: looking. agg-01 pod OOMs in the logs around 2681234200 but restarted and back up. I see sporadic GC pauses (Java sidecar) and some write errors to redis cluster shard 3. attaching tail of application log:
```
[2681234205] WARN kv-cache: write-failed key=shard-3 err=ETIMEDOUT
[2681234212] ERROR aggregator: commit failed after 3 retries
[2681234213] INFO aggregator: consumer paused for backoff=1500ms
```

Sam R: redis shard 3 showing intermittent high p99 latency around same time. ops team alerted.

Marcus B: hypothesis: intermittent redis latency caused aggregator to pause and skip batches, downstream agg windows got incomplete counts and produced undercounts. system then reprocessed later causing late emits which triggered overage detection when reconciler ran.

Priya K: ok mitigation plan: 1) suppress outgoing billing overage emails while we stabilize; 2) promote agg-02 (healthy) to primary for new commits; 3) run immediate reconciliation backfill job for affected window; 4) postmortem later. Agree?

Lena C: customers are already getting overage emails (some small customers). We need to suppress further notif asap and prepare a short comms note. How long to flip suppression?

Marcus B: suppress should be quick. two options: flip feature flag or pause notification worker. I can flip feature flag in config-store. command: `curl -X POST https://config.redwood/api/flags/billing.notify -d '{"enabled":false}'` (will push to env via rollout). ETA ~3-4m to propagate.

Priya K: do it. @Marcus B proceed. I'll also request an immediate manual pause of the notif-queue via ops if flag fails.

Marcus B: executing now.
```
$ curl -s -X POST https://config.redwood/api/flags/billing.notify -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"enabled":false}'
{"status":"ok","propagated_to":3,"ts":2681234632}
```

Marcus B: flag propagated. Confirming notif service received new config and is not sending new emails.

ops-bot: notif-queue paused by ops at 2681234640 (manual override) :white_check_mark:

Lena C: confirmed with support -- no new overage emails in last 5m. preparing a brief note for affected customers.

Sam R: promoting agg-02 to be primary for commits. running graceful failover:
```
$ kubectl -n metering scale deployment metering-agg-01 --replicas=0
$ kubectl -n metering scale deployment metering-agg-02 --replicas=3
```

Sam R: done. routing policy updated to prefer agg-02. observing consumer lag drop on new pods.

Marcus B: starting reconciliation backfill job for window 2681233600-2681234200. running with concurrency 8 to avoid saturating redis. command:
```
$ ./jobs/reconcile --from=2681233600 --to=2681234200 --concurrency=8
started job id=recon-2681234660
```

Priya K: keep an eye on redis shard 3 while backfill runs. if p99 spikes, throttle backfill. Sam, any longer term ops fixes for redis shard?

Sam R: Ops: we detected a noisy neighbor on shard3 (large scan job from analytics). Kicking that job off a maintenance window and will move to different cluster. Also adding 99th-percentile alerts for redis latency and consumer lag.

Marcus B: quick status update 10m in: backfill job processed ~40% of window, delta reduced to ~2.3%. aggregations aligning.

Lena C: customers: support queue shows ~18 tickets referencing overage emails. I've drafted a short message: "We identified a metering processing delay that caused transient overage flags. We suppressed notifications and are reversing incorrect flags. No charges will be applied while we reconcile. We'll follow up with a full postmortem." Sending after triage OK.

Priya K: good. plan to keep notif suppressed until reconciliation completes and counts reconcile to <0.5% drift. update every 15m.

IncidentBot: Status update: incident assigned to Priya K (oncall). Severity remains P1. Links: bridge, runbook: https://runbooks.redwoodinc/metering-drifts

Marcus B: backfill complete. final reconciliation summary:
```
# pre-recon delta: 98,314 (7.99%)
# post-recon delta: 1,904 (0.16%)
# notifications suppressed: true
# customers with sent emails: 18 (manual recall in progress)
```

Sam R: redis shard 3 moved noisy job off cluster, additional capacity added. consumer lag stable <50. p99 redis latency back to normal.

Priya K: great. re-enabling notifications in 5m if metrics hold.

Marcus B: flipping flag back now.
```
$ curl -s -X POST https://config.redwood/api/flags/billing.notify -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"enabled":true}'
{"status":"ok","propagated_to":3,"ts":2681234801}
```

ops-bot: notif-queue resumed at 2681234810

Lena C: support notified customers already affected with message and apology. tracking responses.

Priya K: incident state -> mitigated. Root cause: intermittent redis shard latency from analytics job causing aggregator pause and missed commits leading to undercounts and late emits that triggered overage flags. Action items: 1) Redis cluster hardening + capacity planning (Sam) 2) Add consumer-lag auto-failover and better backpressure handling in aggregator (Marcus) 3) Test notification suppression runbook and confirm config propagation (Product/CS) 4) Postmortem scheduled tomorrow 11:00 PT (owner: Priya).

IncidentBot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 2681234879. Final severity P1 -> mitigated. Postmortem link (pending): https://pm.redwoodinc/postmortems/2681234567
